The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 92c36602fb496808), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 55-56. statement: Let (A0, C0, B0) and p: X → S be the positive triple and fibration obtained in Theorem 7.1. Retain the normalized original periods and the class F of Theorem 6.2. On disjoint disks Uj about the critical values, use the models of Theorem 8.1, with (9.2) Σj = hj ds ∧ dz, A0 = ℜΣj, C0 = xjℜΣj + yjℑΣj, yj ̸= 0, where hj ̸= 0, xj, and yj are constants and z = a + τ(s)b modulo the elliptic period lattice. There are smaller disks U′ j ⋐ Uj and a smooth path of positive closed triples (At, Ct, Bt), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, starting at (A0, C0, B0), with the following properties. (i) Each of the three cohomology classes is constant. The restrictions of At, Ct to the fibers vanish, and the pair equals (A0, C0) on p−1(U′ j) for every t. (ii) The endpoint pair A = A1, C = C1 is invariant under the torus group bundle acting on X◦ by the action-angle translations of A0. This is also the torus action determined by A. (iii) There is a smooth closed invariant two-form Ψ on X◦ such that (9.3) ∫︂ p−1(s) Ψ = 1, Ψ ∧ A = Ψ ∧ C = 0 on X◦ . On each punctured p−1(U′ j \ {sj}) it equals da ∧ db. In particular, Ψ2 vanishes there. 56 OPENAI The fibration and its smaller nodal models remain fixed. All of these choices are made before introducing the parameter ε in the auxiliary-volume construction.
